result.title: VITAL: A Framework for Validating Agentic AI in Pharmaceutical Drug Development and Clinical Trial Operations
result.summary: Current assurance approaches do not establish whether evidence is sufficient to validate, monitor and govern agentic artificial intelligence (AI) within a pharmaceutical context of use. Plausible outputs may conceal failures in retrieval, reasoning, orchestration or human-control points, where reference standards are unavailable. We developed and operationalised VITAL (Validation by Intended use, Traceability, Autonomy and Lifecycle evidence), a validation framework for agents in clinical development, through landscape analysis, regulatory and standards mapping, expert interviews and multi-stakeholder refinement. VITAL integrates context of use, controls, behavioural validation and lifecycle evidence within a risk-adjusted framework. We applied VITAL across epidemiology and treatment-landscape analysis, site selection, enrolment rescue and trial-design trade-off support to translate autonomy, reversibility, transparency and patient impact into proportionate validation activities, evidence requirements and auditable reconstruction of system behaviour. VITAL may inform evidence requirements and lifecycle accountability for higher-risk pharmaceutical uses; evaluation should assess reproducibility across assessors, organisations and system configurations.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 VITAL 框架，以预期用途、可追溯性、自主性与生命周期证据为核心，为药物研发与临床试验运营中的 agentic AI 设计风险分级的行为验证与证据要求，并在多个制药场景中落地。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据是否足以支持结论」「行为可审计重建」的验证思路可能启发 LVR 中 latent 证据充分性与推理链可追溯性的评价目标，但论文不涉及视觉状态或生成机制，联系偏概念层面，可供核查。
